subject: Proposal: Triple-timeband compromise for SE deep-dive with Acme
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Alex Moreno <alex@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: Triple-timeband compromise for SE deep-dive with Acme

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for lining up your architects for the technical deep-dive. I know coordinating across US/EU/APAC windows is a pain, so I sketched a lightweight "triple timeband" compromise that should keep the session live for the majority, with a way for the region that would be outside business hours to join asynchronously + a short live follow-up. Attached: availability grid and a PNG timeband map.

High-level proposal (one 90–100 minute session):
- Start at a UTC anchor so DST shifts are predictable.
- Targeted overlap bands (examples we can pick from):
  * Option A: 15:00 UTC (08:00 PDT / 17:00 CEST / 00:00 JST next day) — favors EU + US early; APAC catches recording + follow up
  * Option B: 16:00 UTC (09:00 PDT / 18:00 CEST / 01:00 JST next day) — slightly later, improves EU participation
  * Option C: 21:00 UTC (14:00 PDT / 23:00 CEST / 06:00 JST next day) — shifts toward late US / early APAC overlap

Fallbacks and continuity:
- If APAC team cannot join live, we’ll record and run a 30-minute live office-hours slot the following business day timed for APAC.
- We recommend locking on a UTC start (no local time conversion in the invite) and explicitly note local equivalents in the calendar description — reduces DST confusion.

Next steps: can you confirm approximate availability windows for your EU architects (CET/CEST) and APAC architects (JST/SGT)? I attached a simple grid you can edit in Drive. If you prefer, we can propose a single concrete slot and push calendar invites.

Thanks,
Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: acme_availability_grid.xlsx (33KB), timezone-overlap-map.png (82KB)

From: Alex Moreno <alex@acme-corp.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 13:01:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Proposal: Triple-timeband compromise for SE deep-dive with Acme

Thanks Rishi — this is helpful. Quick notes from our side:
- Our EU architects are available broadly 09:00–12:00 CEST the week of May 10; they prefer earlier blocks.
- APAC (Tokyo/Singapore) can do after 15:00 JST but will push to next-day for late-night starts.
- We do have a strict policy against meetings after 23:00 local time for senior architects, so the "next-day 01:00 JST" options will be tricky for them.

Can you nudge Option B down 30 minutes or propose a middle ground? If not, we can do Option A and ask APAC to rely on the recording + a 30-min follow-up.

Appreciate the UTC anchor idea — that should help with DST.

Alex
Head of Integrations
Acme Corporation

Subject: Re: Proposal: Triple-timeband compromise for SE deep-dive with Acme

Rishi / team —

Thanks Alex for the quick reply. A couple of pragmatic suggestions from ops that have worked for multi-region customers:

- Pick a firm UTC anchor and publish all local equivalents in the invite; avoid re-publishing when DST flips happen.
- When the ideal live overlap would push a region past 23:00 local, prefer recording + a shorter live APAC sync the next day (30–45 mins).
- Rotate start times for recurring sessions: if this is a single deep-dive, prioritize the region that needs hands-on time the most.

Concrete middle-ground we can offer to Acme this week:
- Final candidate slot: May 10, 16:00 UTC (09:00 PDT / 18:00 CEST / 01:00 JST on May 11) — it is slightly late for APAC, but within policy if we offer a follow-up slot the next business day at 08:00 JST.
- Alternate earlier slot: May 10, 15:30 UTC (08:30 PDT / 17:30 CEST / 00:30 JST) — keeps APAC closer to midnight but still borderline.

Operational asks for Rishi before we lock:
1) Rishi: which of the two candidate UTC anchors do you prefer?
2) Rishi: can you add the recording + an APAC office-hours follow-up to the calendar when you send the invite?

I can own the follow-up office-hours for APAC if we need an internal facilitator.

—Vivek
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
